data.title: Parcel "customs fee" demand – likely phishing/scam
data.case_title: Suspicious customs fee demand for a parcel (likely scam)
data.summary: A sender calling itself "Paketzentrum Musterstadt – Zollabwicklung" claims €38.90 in import VAT and processing fees are due by 9 November 2026 before a parcel from a non-EU country is released, threatening to return or destroy it otherwise. Multiple details in the letter strongly suggest this is a phishing/scam attempt rather than a genuine customs notice.
data.explanation: This letter looks designed to trick you into paying a stranger's bank account: real German customs (Zoll) never asks for direct transfers to a private company, the IBAN given does not pass a basic validity check, contact is offered only via WhatsApp, and the sender's email domain is not an official one. Do not transfer any money and do not reply via the WhatsApp number. Instead, check the tracking status of any parcel you are actually expecting directly with the courier (DHL, DPD, Deutsche Post, etc.) using their official website, and report this message as phishing. If you have genuinely ordered goods from outside the EU, real import charges are usually collected by the courier itself, not by a separate "clearance" company.

items.title: Do not pay the demanded "customs fee" without verifying it first
items.action: Verify the parcel and any real import charges directly with the actual courier or German customs before considering any payment; do not use the bank details or WhatsApp contact given in this letter
items.consequence: The sender claims the parcel will be returned to the sender or destroyed if no payment arrives by the deadline
items.quote: Überweisen Sie 38,90 € bis 09.11.2026. Geht bis dahin keine Zahlung ein, schicken wir die Sendung an den Absender zurück oder vernichten sie kostenpflichtig.

warnings: The payee "Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd." is not a German customs authority; the real Zoll never demands private bank transfers to release parcels, which strongly suggests this is a phishing/scam scheme.
The provided IBAN fails standard IBAN checksum validation, suggesting it is invalid or fabricated.
The sender offers contact only via WhatsApp and uses a non-official-looking email domain (clearance-mail.example), inconsistent with a genuine customs or logistics authority.
The very short payment deadline combined with a threat to destroy or return the parcel is a common pressure tactic used in parcel-scam emails.

The recipient name (Lina Mustermeier) and sender location (Musterstadt/Musterstraße-style names) are common German placeholder/example names, suggesting this may be a mass-distributed template rather than a real, personalised notice.
